raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

At one to four requests with topk-1 EAGLE v2 chains, a decode step on a fast model is a few milliseconds, and a large
share of it is host work and small launches between the per-stage CUDA graphs (draft, target verify, draft extend):
the verify result's three broadcasts, the sampling-info setup, the relay stash and gathers, the draft-extend tail, and
the step graph's input copies. This PR adds one opt-in flag, `--enable-speculative-step-cuda-graph`, which captures the
decode step as one CUDA graph and turns on six pieces that remove that work. With the flag off (the default), each
changed file runs its existing code. The pieces do not depend on any model or on the megakernel layer.

## Modifications

Every piece below is on with `--enable-speculative-step-cuda-graph` and off without it (the default).

| piece | test / bisect override | what it does | outputs |
|---|---|---|---|
| child-graph splice | none (used by the step graph) | a full-backend graph replay inside an active capture is recorded as a child-graph node | unchanged |
| step CUDA graph | none (the flag itself) | each eligible decode step (draft, target verify, draft extend and the eager work between them) is captured once per key and replayed as one CUDA graph; batch size up to 8; the first two steps of each key run the existing path | bitwise (replays equal eager steps) |
| packed verify broadcast | `SGLANG_SPEC_PACKED_VERIFY_BROADCAST` | one collective per broadcast site instead of three | bitwise |
| lean sampled verify | `SGLANG_SPEC_LEAN_SAMPLED_VERIFY` | temperature through a broadcast view; the target-only tree sampling path without the zero-filled `draft_probs` | bitwise |
| fused relay | `SGLANG_SPEC_FUSED_RELAY` | one scatter launch for the relay stash; row views instead of gathered copies for a single request | bitwise |
| fused draft-extend tail | `SGLANG_SPEC_FUSED_DRAFT_EXTEND_TAIL` | a split-row argmax whose last launch also writes the unit probabilities and the DSA seed rows; meant for use with the step graph, which captures it | bitwise |
| fused input copy | `SGLANG_SPEC_STEP_GRAPH_FUSED_INPUT_COPY` | the step graph's input copies in one launch (13 copies at batch size 1) | bitwise |
| chunked verify sampling | `SGLANG_SPEC_CHUNKED_VERIFY_SAMPLING` (under the lean sampled verify) | the target-only sampling kernel split into per-chunk statistics and a finish kernel, with the same floating-point operations in the same order | bitwise |

- One flag: an override that is not set follows the flag as resolved at startup, so a setup that turns the flag off
  (pipeline parallelism, attention DP, topk above 1, ...) turns the six pieces off too. `=0` turns one piece off
  under the flag, for bisecting; `=1` turns it on without the flag, for tests. Each piece keeps its own eligibility
  checks and falls back to the existing code where they fail.
- Credit: the fused relay carries the change proposed in #41170 behind a switch, rebased onto the current FutureMap;
  the fused draft-extend tail uses the two-stage argmax in `row_argmax.py`, the form proposed for the draft argmax in
  #41172. The chunked kernels set their shared memory with `runtime::set_max_dynamic_smem_per_device` (#41147).
- Related PRs, both now on SGLang main (this branch merges it): #45266 adds a Qwen3.5 binding for megakernel plugins,
  runs a plugin's EAGLE draft entries in the draft and draft-extend graphs and captures a megakernel's KV-length
  attention graph variants; without `--enable-nvidia-megakernel` it changes nothing. #45474 moves the host work between
  the Qwen3.5 MTP decode graphs into graphs, into fewer launches or off the critical path, each piece behind a switch
  that defaults to off; among them are post-verify CUDA graphs for the EAGLE verify's sampling, acceptance and commits,
  and a sampled verify result sent in one broadcast instead of three (the idea of this PR's packed verify broadcast; the
  two now share one allocation, see Base below). This PR captures the whole decode step for any model with full decode
  graphs and needs no megakernel; a step that does not replay exactly the three per-stage graphs is never captured and
  runs the existing path.
- Limitation: while `--enable-speculative-step-cuda-graph` is on, `/update_weights_from_disk` with
  `recapture_cuda_graph` is refused before any weight is loaded. The step graph replays the per-stage graphs it
  captured, and a recapture replaces their runners; recapture support is a follow-up.
- Main's verify opt-ins: with `SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH` set (#45474's post-verify graphs run their
  own graphs inside the verify) or `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SPARSE_VERIFY_SAMPLING` set (it picks its top-k branch per batch,
  outside the step graph's key), the launch turns `--enable-speculative-step-cuda-graph` off with a warning naming the
  variable and keeps the per-stage graphs.
- Start-up warm-up: when the flag is on and a step graph runner is active, the HTTP server's start-up sends short
  requests with the sampling that a chat request setting no sampling field resolves to (the chat API's own
  `to_sampling_params` over the model's generation config; the tokenizer manager merges `--preferred-sampling-params`
  into it as into any request), in batches of 1, 2, ..., N requests per DP rank. N is the smallest of 8, the largest
  batch size of the per-stage decode graphs and `--max-running-requests` per DP rank. Each batch is one request with
  distinct 3-token prompts and 64 new tokens; the tokenizer manager sends it to the scheduler in one message, so with
  one DP rank its prompts are prefilled together and decode as one batch. The step graph therefore captures the key of
  every batch size from 1 to N, as client requests without sampling fields produce it, before the server takes
  requests; SGLang's own warm-up request captures the greedy batch-size-1 key. A batch size that still has no
  unconstrained key with the warm-up's sampling flags (greedy, top-k, top-p, min-p) afterwards gets one more batch; if
  it is still missing, a warning names it and its key is captured at first use.
  One log line gives the warm-up's time and each captured key with its memory. The warm-up is skipped with
  `--skip-server-warmup` and in the offline engine, and with `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1` one log line says it is skipped;
  then every key is captured at its first use, as before.
- Start-up cost: with SGLang's own warm-up request, the server handles 1 + N(N+1)/2 requests per DP rank at start-up
  (2 at `--max-running-requests` 1, 37 at 8; one more batch for a missing size); the N(N+1)/2 added ones each have a
  3-token prompt and 64 new tokens. They appear in the server's request metrics like SGLang's own warm-up request, so
  a client that checks for a server with no earlier requests has to allow for them. In the GLM-5.3 runs below
  (8 x B300, TP 8), the warm-up took 7.7 s at `--max-running-requests` 8, on a host where the same build had started
  before, and 49.0 s at `--max-running-requests` 1, on the first start of this build on its host. The step graphs then
  held 394 MB per GPU at `--max-running-requests` 8 (batch sizes 1 to 8 sampled, 372 MB, plus the greedy batch-size-1
  key, 22 MB) and 44 MB at 1.
- Memory: a key is captured only when every rank has free device memory of at least the largest key captured so far
  (256 MiB before the first) plus 1 GiB. If that check fails while PyTorch's caching allocator holds enough unused
  memory on every rank to cover the need, that cache is released once for the key (`torch.cuda.empty_cache()`, at
  most once per key and 32 times per process) and the check is repeated. Otherwise that key's steps run the existing
  path, the capture is retried every 256 steps, and each rank logs the refusal once per key with its free, needed,
  reserved and allocated memory; each release is logged with the free memory before and after it.
  `/get_server_info` reports under `spec_step_cuda_graph` the `memory_refusals` count, the `last_memory_refusal`
  (batch size, greedy or sampled, constrained or not, and those four memory figures), the `cache_releases` count,
  the `captured_keys` (batch size, greedy or sampled, the top-k / top-p / min-p flags, constrained or not, and MB of
  each), the runner's `max_batch_size` and the caching allocator's `num_alloc_retries` and `num_ooms`. Device memory
  in use can grow
  while serving, so a key first met while serving (a greedy batch above 1, a constrained batch, or a batch size the
  start-up warm-up did not capture) may still be refused (see the agentic-trace runs below for the previous
  revision, which captured batch size 1 only at start-up).
- Kernel inventory: `kernels/ops/speculative/__init__.py` registers the fused draft-extend tail
  (`speculative.draft_extend_tail`, Triton, CUDA only) next to `div_argmax`, as `unit/kernels/test_kernels_namespace.py`
  requires of a public kernel entry point.
- Docs: the new flag in `server_arguments.mdx`; the flag, its six pieces and their overrides, the start-up warm-up,
  the memory check and the cache release in `speculative_decoding.mdx`.
- Tests in this PR: `cuda_graph/spec_step/test_child_graph_capture.py`, `cuda_graph/spec_step/test_eagle_step_cuda_graph_runner.py`,
  `unit/managers/test_single_request_relay.py`, `unit/spec/test_spec_step_graph_fused_input_copy.py` (1 GPU),
  `unit/spec/test_eagle_step_cuda_graph_eligibility.py` (with the memory refusal, the cache release, the start-up
  warm-up and the fallback for main's verify opt-ins), `unit/spec/test_simulated_accept_fixed_shape.py`,
  `unit/spec/test_spec_packed_verify_broadcast.py`, `unit/spec/test_spec_step_graph_switches.py` (CPU), one line in
  `unit/spec/test_spec_registry.py`'s fake server arguments, and
  `e2e/models/test_dsa_glm52_nvfp4_tp_mtp_step_graph.py` (4 GPUs, GLM-5.2 NVFP4).
- Kernel tests of the new CUDA kernels (under `test/registered/`, 1 GPU each):

  | file | what it checks |
  |---|---|
  | `kernels/ops/speculative/test_spec_chain_verify_sampling.py` | for chains, `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` three ways (stock, lean, two-launch chunked) returns the same `predicts` / `accept_index` / `accept_token_num` bit for bit over random, flat, peaked and tail-only distributions, edge coins, every vector width, one-chunk vocabularies, a zero-mass row and CUDA graph replay |
  | `kernels/ops/speculative/test_spec_draft_extend_tail.py` | the fused topk-1 draft-extend tail equals the stock statements bit for bit (values, dtypes, shapes, strides) at batch sizes 1, 2 and 8 with vocabulary 154,880: ties at the first / last / random columns, +inf, -inf and NaN rows, select indices from real and forced acceptance, graph replay |
  | `unit/layers/test_next_relay.py` | the relay scatter kernel (`scatter_spec_extras`) at batch sizes 0, 1 and 129 and widths 1, 17 and 2,560, in CUDA graph replay, with dense sources and indices and with sources whose row stride is wider than their width (a column slice of a wider buffer) and a stride-2 index tensor |

Base and revisions: this branch is this PR's commit `3ba3fd1d2e` on SGLang main `dba22e9b68`, a fix that matches
sampling modes in the start-up warm-up's missing-key check (`bcf3db0ab6`, above), a merge of SGLang main `286e018594`,
three commits on top, and merges of SGLang main `00394f9f35` and `9e9296fdf3`:

- The merge of `286e018594` kept both sides of four conflicts: `arg_groups/field_order.py` (main's new fields, then
  `enable_speculative_step_cuda_graph` last), `entrypoints/http_server.py` (this PR's warm-up line for the Rust server,
  then main's `rust_server_sidecar` block), `speculative/spec_utils.py` (main's KV-cache imports and this PR's
  `child_graph_capture` import) and `speculative/eagle_utils.py`: #45474 added the same packed verify broadcast behind
  `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_PACKED_VERIFY_BCAST` (`_verify_outputs`); `eagle_sample` keeps this PR's `_alloc_verify_outputs`
  and `_broadcast_verify_outputs`, and `_alloc_verify_outputs` now allocates through `_verify_outputs`, packed when
  either variable is set, with the same layout.
- Port to main: sgl-project/sglang#46719 records an `eager_on_graph` break at capture without running it, so a break
  returns `None` (sgl-project/sglang#46792 renamed `capture_stub` to `on_capture`): the step graph's grammar mask break
  fills the runner-owned mask and returns `None`, and the child-graph test's break writes into a buffer the test owns.
  #45474 samples the simulated acceptance length with the worker's generator; the step graph's override takes that
  generator and keeps it with the sample's other arguments, so a replay samples with it as the eager step does.
- Three registered CPU tests that already failed with the filed revision now pass: `test_full_cuda_graph_backend`
  (`FullCudaGraphBackend` gets class defaults for `_keep_raw_graph` and `graph_epoch`), `test_backend_resolution`
  (`resolve_decode_backend` reads `enable_speculative_step_cuda_graph` only when the speculative config is published)
  and `test_spec_registry` (its fake server arguments set `enable_speculative_step_cuda_graph=False`).
- The fallback for main's verify opt-ins (above), with a CPU test.
- The merge of `00394f9f35` had no conflict, and no line of this PR changed in it.
- The merge of `9e9296fdf3` had one conflict, in `layers/attention/dsa_backend.py`: main (sgl-project/sglang#45946)
  adds three methods to `DeepseekSparseAttnBackend` that wrap its FlashMLA calls, at the place where this PR adds
  `out_graph_metadata_capturable`. Both are kept, this PR's method first. #45946 also routes the backend's FlashMLA
  calls through the new methods, which call the same functions as before; no line of this PR calls them, and no line
  of this PR changed in the merge.

Earlier revisions: against the revision before it (`9258cb78da`, also on SGLang main `dba22e9b68`), `3ba3fd1d2e`
captures the keys of batch sizes 1 to N at start-up instead of batch size 1
only, releases PyTorch's cached memory once before a refused capture, reports `captured_keys`, `cache_releases` and
`max_batch_size`, and updates the docs and the eligibility tests (5 files). The revision before that (`f35a9e5f82`,
on SGLang main `74c08f3dc5`) had no start-up warm-up, no memory-refusal diagnostics and no kernel-inventory
registration. Apart from those additions, the changes for SGLang main `dba22e9b68` since the revisions measured on SGLang
main `af856717c2` were these:

- `arg_groups/field_order.py` appends `enable_speculative_step_cuda_graph` at the end of `POSITIONAL_FIELD_ORDER`
  (after main's newest field), as main's positional-slot test requires.
- In `managers/overlap_utils.py` the fused relay branch of `stash` comes after main's check that skips the scatter when
  the graph has already published it. That check's relay is not used by the EAGLE chains measured below, so they run
  the same code as before.
- The conflict in `speculative/eagle_utils.py` was resolved with this PR's changed lines as before; main's
  verify-sampling dispatch reaches, on CUDA, the same `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` that this PR extends.
- The `typing` import of `speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py` also takes main's `Callable`.

- GLM-5.3 NVFP4, 3 draft steps, with `--enable-nvidia-megakernel --enable-speculative-step-cuda-graph

- GLM-5.2 NVFP4 with the same flags and 5 draft steps: a regex request and a JSON-schema request (temperature 0) both

After each merge of SGLang main (`00394f9f35`, then `9e9296fdf3`), this branch was checked again on CPU: SGLang's

## Accuracy Tests

GLM-5.3 NVFP4, 8 x B300, TP 8, MTP (EAGLE, 3 steps, topk 1, 4 draft tokens), real acceptance, this PR alone on SGLang
main `af856717c2` (stock attention and MoE). "On" is `--enable-speculative-step-cuda-graph` with the six overrides set
to 1, the same pieces as the flag alone; "off" is the flag off with no override set:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| on vs off, 40 prompts (20 greedy + 20 server-default sampling, incl. constrained tool-call rows; sent by a local script, not part of this PR) | the same tokens on 40 / 40 (two off launches agree on 40 / 40) |
| step graph | captured on 8 / 8 ranks |
| GSM8K-200, on | 0.995, acceptance length 2.994 |
| unit and kernel tests (this PR's unit files other than `test_spec_step_graph_switches.py` + its 3 kernel test files, run on an earlier revision of this PR with an earlier revision of the megakernel hooks PR (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46210) and an earlier version of the HiCache change of sgl-project/sglang#45795 applied), also with `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI=true` | all pass |
| `unit/spec/test_spec_step_graph_switches.py` (CPU: launch arguments parsed, resolved and published as a scheduler process publishes them), also with `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI=true` | passes: the flag alone turns on all six pieces, each override `=0` turns off only its piece, and without the flag (or when startup turns it off) all six are off |
| this revision's CPU tests of the start-up warm-up, the memory refusal and the cache release (`unit/spec/test_eagle_step_cuda_graph_eligibility.py`) and of the kernel inventory (`test_reclassified_public_entry_points_are_inventoried` in `unit/kernels/test_kernels_namespace.py`) | pass: a memory refusal is counted and logged once per key; the cache is released only when it can cover the need, at most once per key and up to a cap, and with enough free memory the check is one collective as before; the warm-up's sampling gives the same capture key as a chat request without sampling fields, for six generation configs; the warm-up captures the keys of batch sizes 1 to N (for example 1 to 4 at `--max-running-requests` 4 and 1 to 8 at 16), one request per batch size k with k distinct prompts per DP rank, gives a missing size one more batch and then a warning (a key of another sampling mode or a constrained key does not count), and sends nothing without an active step graph runner; the draft-extend tail is in the kernel inventory |

The "on" runs above set the six overrides to 1 because they were made on earlier revisions of this PR, in which the
overrides did not yet follow the flag; in this revision the flag alone turns on the same six pieces
(the `test_spec_step_graph_switches.py` row).

On the stack of the unit and kernel test row above, the draft-extend tail and relay scatter files also pass when run
as `python3 <file>` (15 and 18 passed).

On 4 x B300 with this PR alone on SGLang main `af856717c2`, the GLM-5.2 NVFP4 step-graph e2e
(`e2e/models/test_dsa_glm52_nvfp4_tp_mtp_step_graph.py`, 3 tests, real acceptance) passes with the step graph alone

That run used an earlier revision of this PR, in which the flag turned on the step graph alone. With the flag that
also turns on the six pieces, the e2e was rerun with `3ba3fd1d2e` alone on SGLang main `dba22e9b68` (4 x B300): 3
tests OK, GSM8K 0.942, acceptance length 3.97.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Per decode step at one request (`--max-running-requests` 1): GLM-5.3 NVFP4 on 8 x B300, TP 8, MTP (EAGLE, 3 steps,
topk 1, 4 draft tokens), fixed acceptance length 2.99. Stack: SGLang main `af856717c2` with earlier
revisions of this PR and of the megakernel hooks PR (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46210) and an earlier version of the deferred HiCache
ready-count sync now proposed in sgl-project/sglang#45795 (`--hicache-async-ready-sync`), plus an earlier revision of the
sgl-nvidia-mega GLM-5.3 target and draft specs (https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega/pull/24; slots `attention,moe,hops,draft`, embedding replication
on). Workload (a local client script, not part of this PR): a synthetic multi-turn chat with a 253K-token prefix, then a 150-token and a 1,000-token reply;
HiCache write-back with a 270 GB host pool. ms per decode step = the median client-side chunk interval of the
1,000-token reply after its first 50 chunks.

- On: `--enable-speculative-step-cuda-graph` with the six overrides set to 1 (the same pieces as the flag alone).
  Off, for a single piece: that piece's override set to 0, everything else on (for the step CUDA graph row: the flag
  off, the six overrides set to 1). Off, for "all of this PR": the flag off and no override set. The megakernel and
  `--hicache-async-ready-sync` stay on in every run of this table. Without the step graph the fused input copy has
  nothing to copy, and without the lean sampled verify the chunked verify sampling, which runs under it, is off too.
- Order as run, one server launch per run, all on one host: on; all of this PR off, twice; on; the deferred HiCache
  sync flag off, twice (not reported here); on; step CUDA graph off, packed verify broadcast off; on; lean sampled
  verify off, fused relay off; on; fused draft-extend tail off, fused input copy off; on; chunked verify sampling off;
  on.
- "On" is the mean of the two all-on runs just before and after the row's block; "off" is the row's off run (for
  "all of this PR", the mean of its two). The difference is off - on (positive: the piece makes the step shorter),
  computed before rounding.

| piece | ms per decode step, off | on | difference | against the all-on run-to-run range (0.10 ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| all of this PR | 5.53 | 5.41 | +0.12 | larger |
| step CUDA graph | 5.41 | 5.44 | -0.03 | within |
| packed verify broadcast | 5.37 | 5.44 | -0.07 | within |
| lean sampled verify | 5.40 | 5.43 | -0.03 | within |
| fused relay | 5.45 | 5.43 | +0.02 | within |
| fused draft-extend tail | 5.40 | 5.43 | -0.03 | within |
| fused input copy | 5.40 | 5.43 | -0.03 | within |
| chunked verify sampling | 5.44 | 5.45 | -0.01 | within |

The seven all-on runs span 0.10 ms (5.37 to 5.47 ms per step). Only the difference for the whole PR is larger than
that range; each single piece's difference is within it.

On a multi-turn agentic coding trace, the public Hugging Face dataset `semianalysisai/cc-traces-weka-062126` (split
`train`), replayed as recorded (about one hour per run; its requests set no sampling field, so they run with the
server's default sampling): GLM-5.3 NVFP4 on 8 x B300, TP 8, MTP as above, fixed acceptance length 2.99, HiCache
write-back with a 270 GB host pool, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` equal to `--max-running-requests`, SGLang's compiled
Rust radix-tree core in every run. "Stock" is SGLang main `dba22e9b68` with none of the flags below. "All on" is SGLang
main `dba22e9b68` with `3ba3fd1d2e`, the megakernel hooks PR (`465a9dd5b7`), sgl-project/sglang#45795 at its head
`29e8125875` and the GLM-5.3 plugin PR (`ad0bf9103d`), launched with `--enable-nvidia-megakernel
--enable-speculative-step-cuda-graph --hicache-async-ready-sync` and no override set. The servers of each row ran on
one host in one session. Each cell is all on / stock.

In an earlier session on SGLang main `74c08f3dc5`, with an earlier revision of this PR that captured the batch-size-1

detail.body:
## Motivation

At one to four requests with topk-1 EAGLE v2 chains, a decode step on a fast model is a few milliseconds, and a large
share of it is host work and small launches between the per-stage CUDA graphs (draft, target verify, draft extend):
the verify result's three broadcasts, the sampling-info setup, the relay stash and gathers, the draft-extend tail, and
the step graph's input copies. This PR adds one opt-in flag, `--enable-speculative-step-cuda-graph`, which captures the
decode step as one CUDA graph and turns on six pieces that remove that work. With the flag off (the default), each
changed file runs its existing code. The pieces do not depend on any model or on the megakernel layer.

## Modifications

Every piece below is on with `--enable-speculative-step-cuda-graph` and off without it (the default).

| piece | test / bisect override | what it does | outputs |
|---|---|---|---|
| child-graph splice | none (used by the step graph) | a full-backend graph replay inside an active capture is recorded as a child-graph node | unchanged |
| step CUDA graph | none (the flag itself) | each eligible decode step (draft, target verify, draft extend and the eager work between them) is captured once per key and replayed as one CUDA graph; batch size up to 8; the first two steps of each key run the existing path | bitwise (replays equal eager steps) |
| packed verify broadcast | `SGLANG_SPEC_PACKED_VERIFY_BROADCAST` | one collective per broadcast site instead of three | bitwise |
| lean sampled verify | `SGLANG_SPEC_LEAN_SAMPLED_VERIFY` | temperature through a broadcast view; the target-only tree sampling path without the zero-filled `draft_probs` | bitwise |
| fused relay | `SGLANG_SPEC_FUSED_RELAY` | one scatter launch for the relay stash; row views instead of gathered copies for a single request | bitwise |
| fused draft-extend tail | `SGLANG_SPEC_FUSED_DRAFT_EXTEND_TAIL` | a split-row argmax whose last launch also writes the unit probabilities and the DSA seed rows; meant for use with the step graph, which captures it | bitwise |
| fused input copy | `SGLANG_SPEC_STEP_GRAPH_FUSED_INPUT_COPY` | the step graph's input copies in one launch (13 copies at batch size 1) | bitwise |
| chunked verify sampling | `SGLANG_SPEC_CHUNKED_VERIFY_SAMPLING` (under the lean sampled verify) | the target-only sampling kernel split into per-chunk statistics and a finish kernel, with the same floating-point operations in the same order | bitwise |

- One flag: an override that is not set follows the flag as resolved at startup, so a setup that turns the flag off
  (pipeline parallelism, attention DP, topk above 1, ...) turns the six pieces off too. `=0` turns one piece off
  under the flag, for bisecting; `=1` turns it on without the flag, for tests. Each piece keeps its own eligibility
  checks and falls back to the existing code where they fail.
- Credit: the fused relay carries the change proposed in #41170 behind a switch, rebased onto the current FutureMap;
  the fused draft-extend tail uses the two-stage argmax in `row_argmax.py`, the form proposed for the draft argmax in
  #41172. The chunked kernels set their shared memory with `runtime::set_max_dynamic_smem_per_device` (#41147).
- Related PRs, both now on SGLang main (this branch merges it): #45266 adds a Qwen3.5 binding for megakernel plugins,
  runs a plugin's EAGLE draft entries in the draft and draft-extend graphs and captures a megakernel's KV-length
  attention graph variants; without `--enable-nvidia-megakernel` it changes nothing. #45474 moves the host work between
  the Qwen3.5 MTP decode graphs into graphs, into fewer launches or off the critical path, each piece behind a switch
  that defaults to off; among them are post-verify CUDA graphs for the EAGLE verify's sampling, acceptance and commits,
  and a sampled verify result sent in one broadcast instead of three (the idea of this PR's packed verify broadcast; the
  two now share one allocation, see Base below). This PR captures the whole decode step for any model with full decode
  graphs and needs no megakernel; a step that does not replay exactly the three per-stage graphs is never captured and
  runs the existing path.
- Limitation: while `--enable-speculative-step-cuda-graph` is on, `/update_weights_from_disk` with
  `recapture_cuda_graph` is refused before any weight is loaded. The step graph replays the per-stage graphs it
  captured, and a recapture replaces their runners; recapture support is a follow-up.
- Main's verify opt-ins: with `SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH` set (#45474's post-verify graphs run their
  own graphs inside the verify) or `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SPARSE_VERIFY_SAMPLING` set (it picks its top-k branch per batch,
  outside the step graph's key), the launch turns `--enable-speculative-step-cuda-graph` off with a warning naming the
  variable and keeps the per-stage graphs.
- Start-up warm-up: when the flag is on and a step graph runner is active, the HTTP server's start-up sends short
  requests with the sampling that a chat request setting no sampling field resolves to (the chat API's own
  `to_sampling_params` over the model's generation config; the tokenizer manager merges `--preferred-sampling-params`
  into it as into any request), in batches of 1, 2, ..., N requests per DP rank. N is the smallest of 8, the largest
  batch size of the per-stage decode graphs and `--max-running-requests` per DP rank. Each batch is one request with
  distinct 3-token prompts and 64 new tokens; the tokenizer manager sends it to the scheduler in one message, so with
  one DP rank its prompts are prefilled together and decode as one batch. The step graph therefore captures the key of
  every batch size from 1 to N, as client requests without sampling fields produce it, before the server takes
  requests; SGLang's own warm-up request captures the greedy batch-size-1 key. A batch size that still has no
  unconstrained key with the warm-up's sampling flags (greedy, top-k, top-p, min-p) afterwards gets one more batch; if
  it is still missing, a warning names it and its key is captured at first use.
  One log line gives the warm-up's time and each captured key with its memory. The warm-up is skipped with
  `--skip-server-warmup` and in the offline engine, and with `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1` one log line says it is skipped;
  then every key is captured at its first use, as before.
- Start-up cost: with SGLang's own warm-up request, the server handles 1 + N(N+1)/2 requests per DP rank at start-up
  (2 at `--max-running-requests` 1, 37 at 8; one more batch for a missing size); the N(N+1)/2 added ones each have a
  3-token prompt and 64 new tokens. They appear in the server's request metrics like SGLang's own warm-up request, so
  a client that checks for a server with no earlier requests has to allow for them. In the GLM-5.3 runs below
  (8 x B300, TP 8), the warm-up took 7.7 s at `--max-running-requests` 8, on a host where the same build had started
  before, and 49.0 s at `--max-running-requests` 1, on the first start of this build on its host. The step graphs then
  held 394 MB per GPU at `--max-running-requests` 8 (batch sizes 1 to 8 sampled, 372 MB, plus the greedy batch-size-1
  key, 22 MB) and 44 MB at 1.
- Memory: a key is captured only when every rank has free device memory of at least the largest key captured so far
  (256 MiB before the first) plus 1 GiB. If that check fails while PyTorch's caching allocator holds enough unused
  memory on every rank to cover the need, that cache is released once for the key (`torch.cuda.empty_cache()`, at
  most once per key and 32 times per process) and the check is repeated. Otherwise that key's steps run the existing
  path, the capture is retried every 256 steps, and each rank logs the refusal once per key with its free, needed,
  reserved and allocated memory; each release is logged with the free memory before and after it.
  `/get_server_info` reports under `spec_step_cuda_graph` the `memory_refusals` count, the `last_memory_refusal`
  (batch size, greedy or sampled, constrained or not, and those four memory figures), the `cache_releases` count,
  the `captured_keys` (batch size, greedy or sampled, the top-k / top-p / min-p flags, constrained or not, and MB of
  each), the runner's `max_batch_size` and the caching allocator's `num_alloc_retries` and `num_ooms`. Device memory
  in use can grow
  while serving, so a key first met while serving (a greedy batch above 1, a constrained batch, or a batch size the
  start-up warm-up did not capture) may still be refused (see the agentic-trace runs below for the previous
  revision, which captured batch size 1 only at start-up).
- Kernel inventory: `kernels/ops/speculative/__init__.py` registers the fused draft-extend tail
  (`speculative.draft_extend_tail`, Triton, CUDA only) next to `div_argmax`, as `unit/kernels/test_kernels_namespace.py`
  requires of a public kernel entry point.
- Docs: the new flag in `server_arguments.mdx`; the flag, its six pieces and their overrides, the start-up warm-up,
  the memory check and the cache release in `speculative_decoding.mdx`.
- Tests in this PR: `cuda_graph/spec_step/test_child_graph_capture.py`, `cuda_graph/spec_step/test_eagle_step_cuda_graph_runner.py`,
  `unit/managers/test_single_request_relay.py`, `unit/spec/test_spec_step_graph_fused_input_copy.py` (1 GPU),
  `unit/spec/test_eagle_step_cuda_graph_eligibility.py` (with the memory refusal, the cache release, the start-up
  warm-up and the fallback for main's verify opt-ins), `unit/spec/test_simulated_accept_fixed_shape.py`,
  `unit/spec/test_spec_packed_verify_broadcast.py`, `unit/spec/test_spec_step_graph_switches.py` (CPU), one line in
  `unit/spec/test_spec_registry.py`'s fake server arguments, and
  `e2e/models/test_dsa_glm52_nvfp4_tp_mtp_step_graph.py` (4 GPUs, GLM-5.2 NVFP4).
- Kernel tests of the new CUDA kernels (under `test/registered/`, 1 GPU each):

  | file | what it checks |
  |---|---|
  | `kernels/ops/speculative/test_spec_chain_verify_sampling.py` | for chains, `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` three ways (stock, lean, two-launch chunked) returns the same `predicts` / `accept_index` / `accept_token_num` bit for bit over random, flat, peaked and tail-only distributions, edge coins, every vector width, one-chunk vocabularies, a zero-mass row and CUDA graph replay |
  | `kernels/ops/speculative/test_spec_draft_extend_tail.py` | the fused topk-1 draft-extend tail equals the stock statements bit for bit (values, dtypes, shapes, strides) at batch sizes 1, 2 and 8 with vocabulary 154,880: ties at the first / last / random columns, +inf, -inf and NaN rows, select indices from real and forced acceptance, graph replay |
  | `unit/layers/test_next_relay.py` | the relay scatter kernel (`scatter_spec_extras`) at batch sizes 0, 1 and 129 and widths 1, 17 and 2,560, in CUDA graph replay, with dense sources and indices and with sources whose row stride is wider than their width (a column slice of a wider buffer) and a stride-2 index tensor |

Base and revisions: this branch is this PR's commit `3ba3fd1d2e` on SGLang main `dba22e9b68`, a fix that matches
sampling modes in the start-up warm-up's missing-key check (`bcf3db0ab6`, above), a merge of SGLang main `286e018594`,
three commits on top, and merges of SGLang main `00394f9f35` and `9e9296fdf3`:

- The merge of `286e018594` kept both sides of four conflicts: `arg_groups/field_order.py` (main's new fields, then
  `enable_speculative_step_cuda_graph` last), `entrypoints/http_server.py` (this PR's warm-up line for the Rust server,
  then main's `rust_server_sidecar` block), `speculative/spec_utils.py` (main's KV-cache imports and this PR's
  `child_graph_capture` import) and `speculative/eagle_utils.py`: #45474 added the same packed verify broadcast behind
  `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_PACKED_VERIFY_BCAST` (`_verify_outputs`); `eagle_sample` keeps this PR's `_alloc_verify_outputs`
  and `_broadcast_verify_outputs`, and `_alloc_verify_outputs` now allocates through `_verify_outputs`, packed when
  either variable is set, with the same layout.
- Port to main: sgl-project/sglang#46719 records an `eager_on_graph` break at capture without running it, so a break
  returns `None` (sgl-project/sglang#46792 renamed `capture_stub` to `on_capture`): the step graph's grammar mask break
  fills the runner-owned mask and returns `None`, and the child-graph test's break writes into a buffer the test owns.
  #45474 samples the simulated acceptance length with the worker's generator; the step graph's override takes that
  generator and keeps it with the sample's other arguments, so a replay samples with it as the eager step does.
- Three registered CPU tests that already failed with the filed revision now pass: `test_full_cuda_graph_backend`
  (`FullCudaGraphBackend` gets class defaults for `_keep_raw_graph` and `graph_epoch`), `test_backend_resolution`
  (`resolve_decode_backend` reads `enable_speculative_step_cuda_graph` only when the speculative config is published)
  and `test_spec_registry` (its fake server arguments set `enable_speculative_step_cuda_graph=False`).
- The fallback for main's verify opt-ins (above), with a CPU test.
- The merge of `00394f9f35` had no conflict, and no line of this PR changed in it.
- The merge of `9e9296fdf3` had one conflict, in `layers/attention/dsa_backend.py`: main (sgl-project/sglang#45946)
  adds three methods to `DeepseekSparseAttnBackend` that wrap its FlashMLA calls, at the place where this PR adds
  `out_graph_metadata_capturable`. Both are kept, this PR's method first. #45946 also routes the backend's FlashMLA
  calls through the new methods, which call the same functions as before; no line of this PR calls them, and no line
  of this PR changed in the merge.

Earlier revisions: against the revision before it (`9258cb78da`, also on SGLang main `dba22e9b68`), `3ba3fd1d2e`
captures the keys of batch sizes 1 to N at start-up instead of batch size 1
only, releases PyTorch's cached memory once before a refused capture, reports `captured_keys`, `cache_releases` and
`max_batch_size`, and updates the docs and the eligibility tests (5 files). The revision before that (`f35a9e5f82`,
on SGLang main `74c08f3dc5`) had no start-up warm-up, no memory-refusal diagnostics and no kernel-inventory
registration. Apart from those additions, the changes for SGLang main `dba22e9b68` since the revisions measured on SGLang

- `arg_groups/field_order.py` appends `enable_speculative_step_cuda_graph` at the end of `POSITIONAL_FIELD_ORDER`

- The conflict in `speculative/eagle_utils.py` was resolved with this PR's changed lines as before; main's
  verify-sampling dispatch reaches, on CUDA, the same `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` that this PR extends.
- The `typing` import of `speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py` also takes main's `Callable`.

The accuracy results and the per-step table below were measured on SGLang main `af856717c2` with the earlier
revisions each one names. The first agentic-trace table below was measured on SGLang main `dba22e9b68` with `3ba3fd1d2e`,
the megakernel hooks PR at `465a9dd5b7`, sgl-project/sglang#45795 at its head of that time `29e8125875` and the GLM-5.3
plugin PR at `ad0bf9103d`; the other agentic-trace runs below name their revisions. Before those runs,
`3ba3fd1d2e` was checked with the same PRs on one 8-GPU host with dummy weights: at `--max-running-requests` 4 and 8,
the start-up warm-up captured the sampled keys of batch sizes 1 to 4 and 1 to 8 and the greedy batch-size-1 key on
all 8 ranks before the server was ready, and short synthetic loads of 2 and 4 concurrent requests (at 4) and of 4
and 8 (at 8) then replayed every decode step, with no memory refusal and no new key.

On SGLang main `286e018594`, before the merge of `00394f9f35`, this branch was checked with the megakernel hooks PR
(`ba86b681b5`), sgl-project/sglang#45795 (at `6ffe9cd46c`) and the up-to-date GLM-5.3 plugin PR (`b8a85c739b`), on
8 x B300. The GPU checks ran this branch at `0d39d7fdbb`, before the commit with the fallback for main's verify
opt-ins, except the fallback check (the last item), which ran the head of that time. On CPU, this PR's CPU tests
pass, and the registered CPU suites it
touches fail on no test id that does not also fail on SGLang main itself. On the GPU host, this PR's test files (all but the 4-GPU e2e) and `unit/spec/test_spec_registry.py` pass,
each file in its own process, with and without `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI` (0 failed).

- GLM-5.3 NVFP4, 3 draft steps, with `--enable-nvidia-megakernel --enable-speculative-step-cuda-graph
  --hicache-async-ready-sync` at `--max-running-requests` 8: the start-up warm-up captured the sampled keys of batch sizes 1 to 8 and the greedy
  batch-size-1 key on 8 / 8 ranks (37 start-up requests, no memory refusal), and GSM8K-200 (5-shot, greedy) scored
  0.985 / 0.990 at 4 concurrent requests and 0.985 / 0.995 at 8 (all on / stock).
- GLM-5.2 NVFP4 with the same flags and 5 draft steps: a regex request and a JSON-schema request (temperature 0) both
  returned HTTP 200, the first with output that fully matches the regex, the second with output that parses and
  validates against the schema.
- With `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` set (dummy weights): the start-up warm-up ran its 37 requests and captured its keys with

- With `SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH=1` (dummy weights), the server logs
  `enable_speculative_step_cuda_graph disabled: SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH is not supported. Falling back to the per-stage CUDA graphs.`
  and serves every request with the megakernel on and the per-stage graphs; on that head the eligibility test file,
  with its fallback test, also passes on the GPU host with and without `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI`.

After each merge of SGLang main (`00394f9f35`, then `9e9296fdf3`), this branch was checked again on CPU: SGLang's
pre-commit checks pass on this PR's files; on that main, alone and together with the megakernel hooks PR (merged with

with the megakernel hooks PR (merged with the same main), sgl-project/sglang#45795 (at `6ffe9cd46c`) and the GLM-5.3
plugin PR, with GLM-5.3 NVFP4 and the same three flags at `--max-running-requests` 8, at 3 and at 5 draft steps: the

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Record CUDA graph replays as child-graph nodes of an enclosing capture.
+
+While a ``ChildGraphCapture`` is active on the current thread, a graph backend
+hands each graph it would replay to :meth:`ChildGraphCapture.add_graph`. In
+splice mode the graph (captured with ``keep_graph=True``) is added as a
+child-graph node at the capturing stream's current dependencies and becomes
+the stream's only dependency, so work captured afterwards is ordered after it
+(the ``cudaStreamGetCaptureInfo`` / ``cudaStreamUpdateCaptureDependencies``
+pattern). CUDA clones the child when it is added, so the original graph stays
+valid for regular replays. In count mode the graph is launched as usual and
+recorded, together with how far it advanced the CUDA generator, which lets a
+caller check what a region replays before capturing it.
+
+The context also carries named capture overrides: a function decorated with
+:func:`capture_override` calls the handler that the active capture registered
+under that name, and runs unchanged otherwise.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import functools
+from contextvars import ContextVar
+from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, TypeVar
+
+import torch
+
+try:
+    from cuda.bindings import runtime as rt
+except ImportError:
+    rt = None
+
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.runner_backend_utils.breakable_cuda_graph.cuda_utils import (
+    checkCudaErrors,
+)
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.runner_utils.pool import graph_pool_replay_scope
+
+__all__ = [
+    "ChildGraphCapture",
+    "capture_override",
+    "current_child_graph_capture",
+    "splice_graph_into_capture",
+]
+
+_F = TypeVar("_F", bound=Callable[..., Any])
+
+_current_capture_var: ContextVar[Optional[ChildGraphCapture]] = ContextVar(
+    "child_graph_capture", default=None
+)
+
+
+def current_child_graph_capture() -> Optional[ChildGraphCapture]:
+    return _current_capture_var.get()
+
+
+def splice_graph_into_capture(graph: torch.cuda.CUDAGraph, stream: Any) -> None:
+    """Add ``graph`` (captured with ``keep_graph=True``) as a child-graph node
+    of the capture that is active on ``stream``."""
+    if rt is None:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "Splicing CUDA graphs requires the 'cuda-python' package. "
+            "Install it with: pip install cuda-python"
+        )
+    stream_ptr = stream.cuda_stream
+    status, _, capturing_graph, deps, _, num_deps = checkCudaErrors(
+        rt.cudaStreamGetCaptureInfo(stream_ptr)
+    )
+    if status != rt.cudaStreamCaptureStatus.cudaStreamCaptureStatusActive:
+        raise RuntimeError("The current stream is not capturing a CUDA graph")
+    # Raises unless the graph was created with keep_graph=True.
+    child = rt.cudaGraph_t(init_value=graph.raw_cuda_graph())
+    deps = list(deps)[:num_deps]
+    node = checkCudaErrors(
+        rt.cudaGraphAddChildGraphNode(capturing_graph, deps, len(deps), child)
+    )
+    checkCudaErrors(
+        rt.cudaStreamUpdateCaptureDependencies(
+            stream_ptr,
+            [node],
+            None,
+            1,
+            rt.cudaStreamUpdateCaptureDependenciesFlags.cudaStreamSetCaptureDependencies,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+class ChildGraphCapture:
+    """Active-capture context consulted by graph backends and by functions
+    decorated with :func:`capture_override`.
+
+    Args:
+        splice: True to splice graphs into the capture on the current stream;
+            False to launch them as usual and record them.
+        overrides: handlers by override name. A handler is called as
+            ``handler(original_fn, *args, **kwargs)``.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        splice: bool,
+        overrides: Optional[Dict[str, Callable[..., Any]]] = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.splice = splice
+        self.overrides: Dict[str, Callable[..., Any]] = dict(overrides or {})
+        # (owner, owner.graph_epoch) per graph handed over, in call order.
+        self.graph_sources: List[Tuple[Any, Optional[int]]] = []
+        # Count mode: CUDA generator offset advanced by each launch.
+        self.generator_offset_deltas: List[int] = []
+        self._token = None
+
+    @property
+    def num_graphs(self) -> int:
+        return len(self.graph_sources)
+
+    def add_graph(self, graph: torch.cuda.CUDAGraph, owner: Any = None) -> None:
+        """Take over one replay of ``graph``: splice it into the capture, or
+        launch it and record it. ``owner`` (e.g. the graph backend) may carry a
+        ``graph_epoch`` that is recorded with it."""
+        self.graph_sources.append((owner, getattr(owner, "graph_epoch", None)))
+        if self.splice:
+            splice_graph_into_capture(graph, torch.cuda.current_stream())
+            return
+        generator = torch.cuda.default_generators[torch.cuda.current_device()]
+        offset = generator.get_offset()
+        with graph_pool_replay_scope():
+            graph.replay()
+        self.generator_offset_deltas.append(generator.get_offset() - offset)
+
+    def __enter__(self) -> ChildGraphCapture:
+        if _current_capture_var.get() is not None:
+            raise RuntimeError("ChildGraphCapture contexts cannot be nested")
+        self._token = _current_capture_var.set(self)
+        return self
+
+    def __exit__(self, *args: object) -> bool:
+        _current_capture_var.reset(self._token)
+        self._token = None
+        return False
+
+
+def capture_override(name: str) -> Callable[[_F], _F]:
+    """Let an active :class:`ChildGraphCapture` replace the decorated function.
+
+    Outside such a capture, or when it registered no handler under ``name``,
+    the function runs unchanged.
+    """
+
+    def decorator(fn: _F) -> _F:
+        @functools.wraps(fn)
+        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
+            capture = _current_capture_var.get()
+            if capture is not None:
+                handler = capture.overrides.get(name)
+                if handler is not None:
+                    return handler(fn, *args, **kwargs)
+            return fn(*args, **kwargs)
+
+        return wrapper  # type: ignore[return-value]
+
+    return decorator

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""One CUDA graph per EAGLE v2 decode step (``--enable-speculative-step-cuda-graph``).
+
+At small batch sizes an EAGLE v2 decode step is three CUDA graph replays
+(draft, target verify, draft extend) with many small kernels and host work
+between them, so the GPU idles between launches. This runner captures the
+worker's own decode step once per key (batch size, sampling setup and the
+layout of the step's input tensors) and replays it as one graph:
+
+* The capture runs ``EAGLEWorkerV2.forward_batch_generation`` on a copy of the
+  batch whose per-step device tensors are runner-owned static buffers, inside
+  a ``BreakableCUDAGraphCapture`` on a dedicated stream with a private memory
+  pool per key. The three per-stage graphs are spliced in as child-graph nodes
+  (``ChildGraphCapture``); the eager work between them is captured from the
+  same code that runs it on the regular path.
+* A replay copies the live input tensors into the static buffers and launches
+  the graph. Host work that must happen every step runs on the host at replay:
+  the FutureMap publish, the shared-read fence and, in the simulated
+  acceptance benchmarking mode, the acceptance length draw (same function,
+  same host RNG stream, once per step).
+* Constrained decoding: the verify tree is copied to pinned host buffers inside
+  the graph, and the grammar bitmask is built on the host between two graph
+  segments (an ``eager_on_graph`` break), still overlapping the target verify
+  forward; the captured sampling reads the bitmask from a static buffer.
+* Random draws of sampled verification are captured inside the torch graph,
+  whose replay advances the CUDA generator exactly like the eager draws.
+
+A key is captured at its first eligible step after ``_NUM_WARMUP_STEPS``
+regular steps, if every rank has enough free device memory (the largest key
+captured so far plus ``_CAPTURE_MEMORY_HEADROOM``). The last warmup step counts
+the per-stage graph replays; a key whose step does not replay exactly the three
+per-stage graphs is never captured. Any step the runner cannot capture runs the
+regular path; the reason is counted (``/get_server_info``) and logged once, and
+a memory refusal is logged once per key with the free and needed memory.
+
+Device memory in use can grow while serving and leave too little for a later
+capture, so the HTTP server's start-up runs batches of 1 to ``max_batch_size``
+requests with the server's default sampling (``entrypoints/warmup.py``): the
+keys of client requests that send no sampling fields are then captured before
+serving starts, next to the greedy batch-size-1 key of SGLang's own warm-up
+request. A capture refused while serving although PyTorch caches enough unused

+def simulated_accept_index_from_device_length(
+    accept_index: torch.Tensor,
+    predict: torch.Tensor,
+    num_correct_drafts: torch.Tensor,
+    candidates: torch.Tensor,
+    target_predict: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+    spec_steps: int,
+    accept_len: torch.Tensor,
+    simulate_acc_token_mode: str,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``spec_utils.generate_simulated_accept_index`` for an acceptance length
+    that was already drawn and is read from ``accept_len`` (a device int32
+    tensor of shape [1]), so that every shape is independent of its value."""
+    bs = accept_index.shape[0]
+    width = spec_steps + 1
+    cols = torch.arange(width, dtype=torch.int32, device=accept_index.device).view(
+        1, width
+    )
+    length = accept_len.view(1, 1)
+    first = accept_index[:, :1]
+    nodes = first + cols
+    sim_accept_index = torch.where(cols < length, nodes, torch.full_like(nodes, -1))
+    num_correct_drafts.copy_((accept_len - 1).expand_as(num_correct_drafts))
+    if simulate_acc_token_mode != "real-draft-token":
+        predict.fill_(100)  # some legit token id, as the regular path
+        return sim_accept_index
+
+    nodes = nodes.view(-1).long()
+    draft_cols = (cols + 1).clamp(max=candidates.shape[1] - 1).view(-1).long()
+    drafts = candidates[:, draft_cols].to(predict.dtype)
+    bonus = target_predict.gather(1, (length - 1).long().expand(bs, 1))
+    current = predict[nodes].view(bs, width)
+    updated = torch.where(
+        cols < length - 1,
+        drafts,
+        torch.where(cols == length - 1, bonus.to(predict.dtype), current),
+    )
+    predict.index_copy_(0, nodes, updated.view(-1))
+    return sim_accept_index

+def _tp_min(*values: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Element-wise MIN over the TP group (host collective)."""
+    group = get_tp_group()
+    if group.world_size == 1:
+        return tuple(int(v) for v in values)
+    tensor = torch.tensor([int(v) for v in values], dtype=torch.int64)
+    torch.distributed.all_reduce(
+        tensor, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.MIN, group=group.cpu_group
+    )

+def _host_copies_in_capture(stream: torch.cuda.Stream) -> List[Tuple[str, int]]:
+    """("read" | "write", host address) of every copy node in the graph being
+    captured on ``stream`` (child graphs excluded) that touches host memory. A
+    replay would repeat such a copy with the values or addresses of capture time."""
+    from cuda.bindings import runtime as rt
+
+    from sglang.srt.model_executor.runner_backend_utils.breakable_cuda_graph.cuda_utils import (
+        checkCudaErrors,
+    )
+
+    status, _, graph, _, _, _ = checkCudaErrors(
+        rt.cudaStreamGetCaptureInfo(stream.cuda_stream)
+    )
+    if status != rt.cudaStreamCaptureStatus.cudaStreamCaptureStatusActive:
+        return []
+    _, num_nodes = checkCudaErrors(rt.cudaGraphGetNodes(graph, 0))
+    nodes, _ = checkCudaErrors(rt.cudaGraphGetNodes(graph, num_nodes))
+    host_types = (
+        rt.cudaMemoryType.cudaMemoryTypeHost,
+        rt.cudaMemoryType.cudaMemoryTypeUnregistered,
+    )
+    found = []
+    for node in nodes or []:
+        node_type = checkCudaErrors(rt.cudaGraphNodeGetType(node))
+        if node_type != rt.cudaGraphNodeType.cudaGraphNodeTypeMemcpy:
+            continue
+        params = checkCudaErrors(rt.cudaGraphMemcpyNodeGetParams(node))
+        for side, ptr in (
+            ("read", int(params.srcPtr.ptr)),
+            ("write", int(params.dstPtr.ptr)),
+        ):
+            attrs = checkCudaErrors(rt.cudaPointerGetAttributes(ptr))
+            if attrs.type in host_types:
+                found.append((side, ptr))
+    return found
+

+def _check_host_copies(allowed_writes=()) -> None:
+    """Fail the capture if the segment being captured copies from host memory or
+    to host memory other than ``allowed_writes`` (runner-owned pinned buffers)."""
+    for side, ptr in _host_copies_in_capture(torch.cuda.current_stream()):
+        if side == "read" or ptr not in allowed_writes:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"the captured step would {side} host memory at {ptr:#x} "
+                "with its capture-time address or value"
+            )

+# try_small_copy's per-tensor element limit.
+_SMALL_COPY_MAX_NUMEL = 8192
+
+
+def _ranges_overlap(a: List[torch.Tensor], b: List[torch.Tensor]) -> bool:
+    def span(t):
+        storage = t.untyped_storage()
+        return storage.data_ptr(), storage.data_ptr() + storage.nbytes()
+
+    spans = sorted(span(t) for t in b if t.numel())
+    for t in a:
+        if not t.numel():
+            continue
+        lo, hi = span(t)
+        if any(s < hi and lo < e for s, e in spans):
+            return True
+    return False
+

+def _copy_step_inputs(
+    static_inputs: List[torch.Tensor],
+    live_inputs: List[torch.Tensor],
+    small_copy=None,
+) -> str:
+    """Copy a replay's live inputs into the graph's static input buffers.
+
+    With ``small_copy`` (``SGLANG_SPEC_STEP_GRAPH_FUSED_INPUT_COPY``) the copies
+    are one launch when every tensor qualifies for it ("fused"); otherwise the
+    small tensors are one launch and the others one copy each ("partial", only
+    when no live tensor shares memory with a static buffer, so the order of the
+    copies cannot matter); otherwise one copy per tensor ("per_tensor").
+    """
+    if small_copy is not None:
+        if small_copy(static_inputs, live_inputs):
+            return "fused"
+        small = [
+            i for i, t in enumerate(static_inputs) if t.numel() <= _SMALL_COPY_MAX_NUMEL
+        ]
+        if 2 <= len(small) < len(static_inputs) and not _ranges_overlap(
+            static_inputs, live_inputs
+        ):
+            if small_copy(
+                [static_inputs[i] for i in small], [live_inputs[i] for i in small]
+            ):
+                chosen = set(small)
+                # One copy_ per tensor, as torch._foreach_copy_ does for a
+                # mixed-dtype list (a same-dtype list would take its fused
+                # path, which is not a plain byte copy).
+                for i in range(len(static_inputs)):
+                    if i not in chosen:
+                        static_inputs[i].copy_(live_inputs[i], non_blocking=True)
+                return "partial"
+    torch._foreach_copy_(static_inputs, live_inputs, non_blocking=True)
+    return "per_tensor"
+

+class _GrammarStep:
+    """Capture-time overrides and replay-time host work of constrained decoding."""
+
+    def __init__(self, runner: EagleStepCudaGraphRunner):
+        self.runner = runner
+        self.host_tree: Optional[Tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]] = None
+        self.tree_ready = torch.cuda.Event()
+        self.mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+
+    def overrides(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+        return {
+            "spec_grammar_tree_from_device": self.tree_from_device,
+            "spec_grammar_vocab_mask": self.vocab_mask,
+        }
+
+    def tree_from_device(
+        self, original, cls, retrieve_next_token, retrieve_next_sibling, draft_token
+    ):
+        tensors = (retrieve_next_token, retrieve_next_sibling, draft_token)
+        # Runner-owned pinned buffers, refilled by every replay.
+        self.host_tree = tuple(
+            torch.empty(t.shape, dtype=t.dtype, pin_memory=True) for t in tensors
+        )
+        for host, tensor in zip(self.host_tree, tensors):
+            host.copy_(tensor, non_blocking=True)
+        _check_host_copies({host.data_ptr() for host in self.host_tree})
+        eager_on_graph(self._record_tree_ready)()
+        return cls(self.host_tree, None)
+
+    def _record_tree_ready(self) -> None:
+        self.tree_ready.record()
+
+    def vocab_mask(self, original, *, reqs, tree, sampling_info, device, barrier):
+        grammar = reqs[0].grammar
+        host_mask = grammar.allocate_vocab_mask(
+            vocab_size=sampling_info.vocab_size,
+            batch_size=self.host_tree[2].numel(),
+            device="cpu",
+        )
+        self.mask = torch.empty(host_mask.shape, dtype=host_mask.dtype, device=device)
+        sampling_info.grammar_mask = None
+        _check_host_copies()
+        eager_on_graph(self._build_mask)()
+        return GrammarMask(grammar, self.mask)
+
+    def _build_mask(self) -> None:
+        # Same steps as spec_utils.build_grammar_vocab_mask, on the live batch, into
+        # the runner-owned mask (a graph break returns None).
+        from sglang.srt.speculative.spec_utils import generate_token_bitmask
+
+        batch = self.runner._live_batch
+        barrier = self.runner._live_grammar_barrier
+        if barrier is not None:
+            barrier()
+        self.tree_ready.synchronize()
+        vocab_mask, _ = generate_token_bitmask(
+            batch.reqs, *self.host_tree, batch.sampling_info.vocab_size
+        )
+        self.mask.copy_(vocab_mask, non_blocking=True)
+        batch.sampling_info.grammar_mask = None

+        if batch.return_hidden_states:

+            return "pipeline proxy tensors"
+        if batch.has_grammar:

+        if batch.hisparse_coordinator is not None:

+        if reason not in self._fallbacks:
+            logger.info(
+                "Speculative step CUDA graph: running the regular step (%s); "
+                "logged once per reason.",
+                reason,
+            )

+    def try_replay(
+        self,
+        batch: ScheduleBatch,
+        on_publish=None,
+        grammar_barrier=None,
+        pp_proxy_tensors=None,
+    ) -> Optional[GenerationBatchResult]:
+        """Run this decode step as one graph. Returns None when the caller must
+        run the regular step instead."""
+        if self._in_worker_call or self.disabled_reason is not None:
+            return None
+        self._num_steps_seen += 1
+        reason = self._ineligible_reason(batch, pp_proxy_tensors)
+        if reason is not None:
+            self._fallback(reason)
+            return None
+        step_tensors = _step_tensors(batch)
+        key = self._key(batch, step_tensors)

+        step = self._steps.get(key)
+        if step is not None:
+            if all(
+                backend.graph_epoch == epoch for backend, epoch in step.stage_graphs
+            ):
+                return self._replay(step, batch, on_publish, grammar_barrier)
+            self._reset("the per-stage CUDA graphs were recaptured")
+
+        reason = self._uncapturable.get(key)
+        if reason is not None:
+            self._fallback(reason)
+            return None

+"""Splicing captured CUDA graphs into an enclosing capture as child-graph nodes.
+
+Covers ``runner_backend_utils/child_graph_capture.py`` through the splice point
+in ``FullCudaGraphBackend.replay`` (each stage graph below is held by a real
+backend):
+  * three graphs spliced between captured glue ops replay bitwise equal to
+    launching them one by one, with fresh inputs on every replay, as one
+    segment;
+  * an eager break (``eager_on_graph``) between two splices runs on every
+    replay;
+  * count mode launches the graphs and records each one with its owner's
+    ``graph_epoch`` and the CUDA generator offset it advanced;
+  * ``capture_override`` dispatch; splicing outside a capture and nesting
+    contexts fail loudly.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+N = 4096
+NUM_REPLAYS = 20
+
+
+class _Stage:
+    """One keep_graph graph (static input ``inp``) held by a FullCudaGraphBackend
+    and replayed through ``FullCudaGraphBackend.replay``."""
+
+    def __init__(self, fn, pool, stream):
+        from sglang.srt.model_executor.runner_backend.full_cuda_graph_backend import (
+            FullCudaGraphBackend,
+        )
+
+        self.inp = torch.zeros(N, device="cuda")
+        for _ in range(2):
+            fn(self.inp)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph(keep_graph=True)
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph, pool=pool, stream=stream):
+            out = fn(self.inp) * 1.0
+        graph.instantiate()
+        self.backend = FullCudaGraphBackend.__new__(FullCudaGraphBackend)
+        self.backend._graphs, self.backend._outputs = {"k": graph}, {"k": out}
+        self.backend._keep_raw_graph, self.backend.graph_epoch = True, 1
+        self.graph = graph
+
+    def replay(self):
+        return self.backend.replay("k", None)
+
+
+class TestChildGraphCapture(CustomTestCase):
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+            raise unittest.SkipTest("CUDA not available")
+        try:
+            from cuda.bindings import runtime  # noqa: F401
+        except ImportError:
+            raise unittest.SkipTest("cuda-python not available")
+
+        from sglang.srt.model_executor.runner_backend_utils.breakable_cuda_graph.breakable_cuda_graph import (
+            BreakableCUDAGraph,
+            BreakableCUDAGraphCapture,
+            eager_on_graph,
+        )
+        from sglang.srt.model_executor.runner_backend_utils.child_graph_capture import (
+            ChildGraphCapture,
+            capture_override,
+            current_child_graph_capture,
+            splice_graph_into_capture,
+        )
+
+        cls.BreakableCUDAGraph = BreakableCUDAGraph
+        cls.BreakableCUDAGraphCapture = BreakableCUDAGraphCapture
+        cls.eager_on_graph = staticmethod(eager_on_graph)
+        cls.ChildGraphCapture = ChildGraphCapture
+        cls.capture_override = staticmethod(capture_override)
+        cls.current_child_graph_capture = staticmethod(current_child_graph_capture)
+        cls.splice_graph_into_capture = staticmethod(splice_graph_into_capture)
+

+        pool, stream = torch.cuda.graph_pool_handle(), torch.cuda.Stream()

+            _Stage(lambda x: torch.cumsum(x, 0), pool, stream),
+            _Stage(lambda x: x * x - 0.5, pool, stream),

+        self.y = torch.zeros(N, device="cuda")
+        # An eager break writes into a buffer its caller owns (it returns None).
+        self.brk = torch.zeros(N, device="cuda")
+        self.coins = torch.zeros(8, device="cuda")
+

+        break between the first two replays and a random draw after the first)."""
+        s1, s2, s3 = self.stages
+        t0 = self.x * 3.0

+            self.coins.copy_(torch.rand(8, device="cuda"))

+            host_break(mid, self.brk)
+            mid = self.brk
+        s2.inp.copy_(mid)
+        o2 = s2.replay()
+        s3.inp.copy_(o2 - o1)
+        o3 = s3.replay()

+
+A fake worker has the shape of an EAGLE v2 decode step: three per-stage graphs

+them (including a GEMM). Driving it through ``EagleStepCudaGraphRunner.
+try_replay`` at batch sizes 1 and 2:
+  * each batch size is captured once (after the warm-up steps) and every step,
+    replayed through the 2-slot output ring, equals the eager step bitwise;
+  * recapturing the stage graphs (a graph epoch change) drops every key
+    together: one reset, and only the key in use is captured again;
+  * recapture-then-replay: a weight update that asks for a recapture (which
+    would build new stage backends the step graph does not track) is refused
+    while the step graph is on, so later steps still replay and equal eager.

+    def run(self, x):

+class _Worker:
+    """Three stage graphs with eager work between them."""
+
+    speculative_num_steps = 3
+
+    def __init__(self, a, w, stages=None):
+        self.stages = stages or [
+            _Stage(lambda x: x.sin() + 1.0),

+"""Chain verify sampling: the lean target-only path and its two-launch form give the same bits.
+
+For chains, ``tree_speculative_sampling_target_only`` is called three ways that must
+return the same predicts / accept_index / accept_token_num:
+
+* with a zero-filled ``draft_probs`` (the stock call),
+* with ``draft_probs=None`` (``SGLANG_SPEC_LEAN_SAMPLED_VERIFY``),
+* with ``draft_probs=None, chunked=True`` (``SGLANG_SPEC_CHUNKED_VERIFY_SAMPLING``: the
+  two vocabulary passes over one CTA per chunk),
+
+over accept / reject at every position, edge coins (0 and the largest float below 1),
+flat, tail-only and zero-mass rows (the last-valid-index fallback), every vector width
+(vocab sizes with gcd(4, vocab) = 4 / 2 / 1) and a one-chunk vocabulary; the chunked
+form also under CUDA-graph replay. Dividing the logits by each request's temperature
+through a broadcast view gives the same probabilities as the expanded temperatures.
+"""

+def _run(probs, candidates, coins, final, draft_probs, chunked, out=None):
+    bs, n, _ = probs.shape
+    if out is None:
+        out = (
+            torch.empty(bs * n, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+            torch.empty((bs, n), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+            torch.empty((bs,), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+        )
+    predicts, accept_index, accept_num = out
+    predicts.fill_(-7)
+    accept_index.fill_(-1)
+    accept_num.fill_(-7)
+    index = torch.arange(bs * n, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64).view(bs, n)
+    next_token = torch.arange(1, n + 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64).repeat(bs, 1)
+    next_token[:, -1] = -1
+    tree_speculative_sampling_target_only(
+        predicts=predicts,
+        accept_index=accept_index,
+        accept_token_num=accept_num,
+        candidates=candidates,
+        retrive_index=index,
+        retrive_next_token=next_token,
+        retrive_next_sibling=torch.full((bs, n), -1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64),
+        uniform_samples=coins,
+        uniform_samples_for_final_sampling=final,
+        target_probs=probs,
+        draft_probs=draft_probs,
+        deterministic=True,
+        chunked=chunked,
+    )

+
+
+def _candidates(probs, gen, accept_rate=0.6):
+    """Per position the target's top token (likely accepted) or a random one."""
+    bs, n, vocab = probs.shape
+    top = probs.argmax(-1)
+    rand_tok = torch.randint(0, vocab, (bs, n), device="cuda", generator=gen)
+    pick = torch.rand((bs, n), device="cuda", generator=gen) < accept_rate
+    candidates = torch.where(pick, top, rand_tok).to(torch.int64)
+    candidates[:, 1:] = torch.where(pick[:, :-1], top[:, :-1], rand_tok[:, 1:])
+    return candidates
+
+
+def _coins(bs, n, mode, gen):
+    if mode == "rand":
+        return (
+            torch.rand((bs, n), device="cuda", generator=gen),
+            torch.rand((bs,), device="cuda", generator=gen),
+        )
+    value = 0.0 if mode == "zero" else 1.0 - 2**-24
+    return (

+        torch.full((bs,), value, device="cuda"),

+
+    def test_chunked_cuda_graph_replay(self):
+        gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(21)
+        bs, n = 2, 4

+def _logits(bs, case, gen):
+    x = torch.randn(bs, VOCAB, generator=gen, device="cuda")

+        if kind == 1:  # tie at the first and last column
+            x[r, 0] = x[r, -1] = x[r].max() + 1
+        elif kind == 2:  # tie at random columns
+            cols = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (3,), generator=gen, device="cuda")
+            x[r, cols] = x[r].max() + 1
+        elif kind == 3:
+            x[r, VOCAB // 3] = float("inf")
+        elif kind == 4:
+            x[r] = float("-inf")
+        elif kind == 5:
+            x[r, VOCAB - 7] = float("nan")
+        elif kind == 6:
+            x[r, 5] = float("nan")
+            x[r, 9] = float("nan")
+        elif kind == 7:

+        for _, b in fields:

+        dsa_topk_indices=(
+            torch.randint(0, 1 << 20, (bs, DSA), device="cuda", generator=g).int()
+            if extra

+    indices = torch.randperm(SLOTS, device="cuda")[:bs]

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("bs", [1, 2])

+            ]

+    for k, _ in FIELDS:
+        _same(resolved[0][k], resolved[1][k])
+    assert views == [bs == 1 and same] * len(FIELDS)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))

+class _FakeDevice:
+    """One rank's device memory as the runner reads it. A capture takes
+    ``capture_bytes``; releasing the cache returns ``releasable`` of the unused
+    reserved memory (unused blocks of live graph pools stay)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, free, reserved=0, allocated=0, releasable=1.0):
+        self.free, self.reserved, self.allocated = free, reserved, allocated
+        self.releasable = releasable
+        self.capture_bytes = 22 * MiB
+        self.empty_cache_calls = 0
+
+    def empty_cache(self):
+        self.empty_cache_calls += 1
+        released = int((self.reserved - self.allocated) * self.releasable)
+        self.free += released
+        self.reserved -= released
+
+    def capture(self):
+        self.free -= self.capture_bytes
+        self.reserved += self.capture_bytes
+        self.allocated += self.capture_bytes
+
+    @contextlib.contextmanager
+    def patched(self):
+        cuda = torch.cuda
+        with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
+            for target, name, kwargs in (
+                (cuda, "mem_get_info", dict(side_effect=lambda: (self.free, 0))),
+                (cuda, "memory_reserved", dict(side_effect=lambda: self.reserved)),
+                (cuda, "memory_allocated", dict(side_effect=lambda: self.allocated)),
+                (cuda, "empty_cache", dict(side_effect=self.empty_cache)),
+                (cuda, "synchronize", {}),
+                (cuda, "is_current_stream_capturing", dict(return_value=False)),
+                (cuda, "stream", dict(side_effect=lambda s: contextlib.nullcontext())),
+                (
+                    runner_module,
+                    "get_tp_group",
+                    dict(return_value=SimpleNamespace(barrier=lambda: None)),
+                ),
+            ):
+                stack.enter_context(mock.patch.object(target, name, **kwargs))
+            tp_min = stack.enter_context(
+                mock.patch.object(runner_module, "_tp_min", side_effect=lambda *v: v)

+class _FakeServer:
+    """The tokenizer manager of a server with one scheduler. The prompts of one
+    request are prefilled together and decode as one batch through the
+    runner's step path; every step gives each request the most tokens a step
+    can (the fewest steps). ``split`` lists batch sizes whose first batch
+    does not form, and ``never`` those that never form."""
+
+    def __init__(self, runner, max_running_requests, split=(), never=()):
+        self.runner = runner
+        self.preferred_sampling_params = None
+        self.max_running_requests = max_running_requests
+        self.split, self.never = set(split), set(never)
+        self.model_config = SimpleNamespace(
+            get_default_sampling_params=lambda: {"top_p": 0.95}
+        )
+        self.requests = []
+        self.state_reads = 0
+
+    async def get_internal_state(self):
+        self.state_reads += 1
+        state = {"effective_max_running_requests_per_dp": self.max_running_requests}
+        if self.runner is not None:
+            state["spec_step_cuda_graph"] = self.runner.stats()
+        return [state]
+
+    async def generate_request(self, req, request):
+        self.requests.append(req)
+        bs = len(_prompts(req))
+        if bs in self.split:
+            self.split.discard(bs)
+        elif bs not in self.never:
+            tokens_per_step = self.runner.worker.speculative_num_steps + 1
+            batch = _batch(bs)
+            (
+                batch.sampling_info.is_all_greedy,
+                batch.sampling_info.need_top_p_sampling,
+                batch.sampling_info.need_top_k_sampling,
+                batch.sampling_info.need_min_p_sampling,
+            ) = _key_flags(req.sampling_params)
+            for _ in range(req.sampling_params["max_new_tokens"] // tokens_per_step):
+                self.runner.try_replay(batch)
+        yield {}

+"""The step CUDA graph's fixed-shape simulated acceptance equals the regular one.
+
+``simulated_accept_index_from_device_length`` reads an already drawn acceptance
+length from a device tensor so that a captured step does not freeze it. For
+every length, both token modes and several batch sizes it must produce exactly
+what ``spec_utils.generate_simulated_accept_index`` produces for that length:
+the accept index (whose shape never depends on the length),
+``num_correct_drafts`` and every element of ``predict``.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.speculative.eagle_step_cuda_graph_runner import (
+    simulated_accept_index_from_device_length,
+)
+from sglang.srt.speculative.spec_utils import generate_simulated_accept_index
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+SPEC_STEPS = 3
+NUM_DRAFT_TOKENS = SPEC_STEPS + 1
+
+
+def _inputs(bs: int, seed: int):
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    width = NUM_DRAFT_TOKENS
+    accept_index = torch.full((bs, width), -1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    accept_index[:, 0] = torch.arange(bs, dtype=torch.int32) * width
+    num_accepted = torch.randint(0, width, (bs,), generator=gen)
+    for row in range(bs):
+        for col in range(1, int(num_accepted[row]) + 1):
+            accept_index[row, col] = row * width + col
+    predict = torch.randint(0, 1000, (bs * width,), dtype=torch.int32, generator=gen)
+    num_correct_drafts = num_accepted.to(torch.int32)
+    candidates = torch.randint(0, 1000, (bs, width), dtype=torch.int64, generator=gen)
+    target_predict = torch.randint(
+        0, 1000, (bs, width), dtype=torch.int64, generator=gen
+    )
+    return accept_index, predict, num_correct_drafts, candidates, target_predict
+
+
+class TestSimulatedAcceptFixedShape(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_matches_regular_path_for_every_length(self):
+        for mode in ("real-draft-token", "fixed"):
+            for bs in (1, 2, 3, 4):
+                for length in range(1, SPEC_STEPS + 2):
+                    with self.subTest(mode=mode, bs=bs, length=length):
+                        ref = _inputs(bs, seed=bs * 31 + length)
+                        got = _inputs(bs, seed=bs * 31 + length)
+                        # match-expected with an integral mean always draws it.
+                        ref_index = generate_simulated_accept_index(
+                            accept_index=ref[0],
+                            predict=ref[1],
+                            num_correct_drafts=ref[2],
+                            candidates=ref[3],
+                            target_predict=ref[4],
+                            bs=bs,
+                            spec_steps=SPEC_STEPS,
+                            simulate_acc_len=float(length),
+                            simulate_acc_method="match-expected",
+                            simulate_acc_token_mode=mode,
+                        )
+                        got_index = simulated_accept_index_from_device_length(
+                            *got,
+                            SPEC_STEPS,
+                            torch.tensor([length], dtype=torch.int32),
+                            mode,
+                        )
+                        self.assertEqual(got_index.dtype, ref_index.dtype)
+                        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(got_index, ref_index))
+                        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(got[1], ref[1]))
+                        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(got[2], ref[2]))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+
+WIDTH = 4
+
+
+class _RecordingGroup:
+    def __init__(self, world_size: int):
+        self.world_size = world_size
+        self.calls = []
+
+    def broadcast(self, tensor, src=0):
+        self.calls.append((tensor.data_ptr(), tensor.numel(), src))

+                    got = _alloc_verify_outputs(bs * WIDTH, bs, WIDTH, "cpu")

+                for r, g in zip(ref[1:3], got[1:3]):
+                    self.assertEqual((r.shape, r.dtype), (g.shape, g.dtype))
+                    self.assertTrue(torch.equal(r, g))

+                self.assertEqual(got[3].shape, ref[3].shape)
+                base = packed.data_ptr()
+                sizes = [t.numel() * t.element_size() for t in got[1:]]
+                offsets = [t.data_ptr() - base for t in got[1:]]
